title: Interval sieve with phase-estimation Fourier sampling (Kuperberg-type, index 1/2)

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the interval-sieve algorithm of proof.md (phase-estimation Fourier sampling with one reused phase-gradient register, integer-label interval sieve with at most ell = ceil(sqrt(n)) bucket bits per stage, interval-shrinking decoding, and the exhaustive shift test for n < 64) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4. In the challenge model its worst-case total work is T(N,s) = O(2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) n^4), with absolute constants, uniformly over all instances of bit length n; the envelope B_T(n) = 2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) n^4 has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds for one fixed configuration on every execution branch, jointly with the other three resource bounds and with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 (in particular at least 2/3).

For the same interval-sieve algorithm of proof.md (phase-estimation Fourier sampling with one reused phase-gradient register, integer-label interval sieve with at most ell = ceil(sqrt(n)) bucket bits per stage, interval-shrinking decoding, and the exhaustive shift test for n < 64), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) n) bits with an absolute constant; the envelope B_C(n) = 2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds for one fixed configuration on every execution branch, jointly with the other three resource bounds and with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 (in particular at least 2/3).

For the same interval-sieve algorithm of proof.md (phase-estimation Fourier sampling with one reused phase-gradient register, integer-label interval sieve with at most ell = ceil(sqrt(n)) bucket bits per stage, interval-shrinking decoding, and the exhaustive shift test for n < 64), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^((41/8) sqrt(n))) qubits with an absolute constant; the envelope B_Q(n) = 2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds for one fixed configuration on every execution branch, jointly with the other three resource bounds and with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 (in particular at least 2/3).

For the same interval-sieve algorithm of proof.md (phase-estimation Fourier sampling with one reused phase-gradient register, integer-label interval sieve with at most ell = ceil(sqrt(n)) bucket bits per stage, interval-shrinking decoding, and the exhaustive shift test for n < 64), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including discarded copies, failed attempts and the final shift tests, is O(2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) n) with an absolute constant; the envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((41/8) sqrt(n)) n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds for one fixed configuration on every execution branch, jointly with the other three resource bounds and with unconditional full-secret success probability at least 3/4 (in particular at least 2/3).

For the same interval-sieve algorithm of proof.md (phase-estimation Fourier sampling with one reused phase-gradient register, integer-label interval sieve with at most ell = ceil(sqrt(n)) bucket bits per stage, interval-shrinking decoding, and the exhaustive shift test for n < 64), the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 3/4 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
